title: An AI agent with its own computer
one: An agent with its own Mac.
tagline: An open-source agent running inside its own macOS virtual machine — it does real work on a real computer, and messages me on WhatsApp.
story: I gave an AI agent its own computer: the open-source Agent Zero framework running inside a dedicated macOS VM (Tart, 8 cores, 8 GB), safely walled off from my machine. It reaches me over WhatsApp, and I put it to work on the least fun job I know — the career pipeline: a multi-user job-search system with contact enrichment and outreach automation. It's the personal twin of the agent-isolation work I do professionally.
why: Shows I can stand up, isolate, and operate autonomous agents on real machines — the same discipline as my platform work, on my own hardware.

title: Centuries-old texts, answering with citations
tagline: A RAG search engine over 73K+ vectors of books, digests, podcasts, and video — with answers that cite their sources down to the page and the timestamp.
story: I built a full-stack search engine for a community's library of esoteric texts and recordings: 73K+ vectors from books, digests, symposiums, podcasts, and YouTube. Ask a question and it answers with receipts — the PDF viewer jumps to the exact page and highlights it; the audio and video players seek to the exact moment. Around it I've shipped App Store apps for the same community, including a guided vowel-practice app and a parenting platform. It's my favorite proof that retrieval is only half the product — the other half is trust.
why: A complete, public, end-to-end RAG product — retrieval, citation UX, a test suite, analytics — not a demo notebook.

title: One universe: stories, a game, an AR scanner
tagline: A storytelling universe spanning a 3D web world, a published iOS game, and an AR room scanner that a city transportation department put to work.
story: Ethereal Dimension started as an AI storytelling platform — interactive narratives inside Three.js worlds — and grew a real-world arm: an AR scanner built on RoomPlan and ARKit that captures spaces in 3D, plus a computer-vision system for real-time barricade detection built with the Austin Department of Transportation. The same universe shipped Hylios, a hand-crafted SpriteKit game on the App Store. It's where my creative work and my spatial-computing work live in one place.
why: Proves range for an AI+iOS portfolio: ARKit/RoomPlan spatial computing, shipped App Store products, and a distinctive creative brand in one coherent world.

At work I built Dynamic Island and Live Activities infrastructure for Venmo; Flow is where I push the same surface as far as it will go, in public, on my own terms.

title: Automation that checks its own work
tagline: A Swift automation system that drives real mobile and browser surfaces — and validates every run against what actually happened on screen.
story: ScrollTracker is a private automation rig I keep sharpening: it operates real mobile and browser surfaces end to end, then verifies each run against the live surface instead of trusting its own logs. Building it has taught me more about real-world automation — timing, state drift, recovery — than any test suite, and that reliability discipline feeds straight back into my agent work. The code stays private; the case study is the capability.
why: Hard-won, real-world automation and validation engineering — the unglamorous reliability work that trustworthy agent systems are made of.
sanitizationNote: Held back on purpose: the repo stays private, and the public card names no automation targets, employers, platforms, or volumes — capability-level description only. Any demo media must be abstracted (blurred or mock surfaces) before publishing.

title: The proof rail: 28+ hackathons, 2 firsts
tagline: The proof section: hackathons across six-plus countries, two first-place wins, and one build that ended up in a BBC documentary.
story: Hackathons are where I check that I can still go zero-to-demo in a weekend. The reel: a drone search-and-rescue system that won MLH at Bloomberg London and was featured in a BBC documentary; ARon, a solo-built AR fitness coach at HackZurich; Carly, a voice-controlled AR car configurator that finished top of 400+; and Elate, a first-place win with a five-person crew at HackZurich 2022. Between builds I've judged Hack Yale twice and mentored at PennApps — and turned the same energy toward community with a game that teaches Sikh langar traditions.
why: A durable, documented pattern of fast prototyping, winning under constraints, and giving back as judge and mentor — the origin story of the applied-AI work.
